When not in use, the Hand-Controllers are designed to "nest" in the well
You have purchased the finest video game system on the market today.

notes: Computer History Museum catalog record: CHM labels its dimensions 'w x h x l' and prints inches and cm; mapped w->width, h->height, l->depth, and the museum's own cm figure is recorded x10 in mm (a decimal shift, no conversion of ours). Record 102662898, 'Fairchild “Channel F” Video Entertainment Computer', 1976 (Made), model FVE100; its description names the console with its permanently attached controllers, AC adapter and TV cable (the bare device, not a boxed set). The record's weight '8 (lb)' is whole pounds: mass_g null.

Quotes from an archive.org scan of the maker's own printed manual are taken from the scan's OCR text layer (the item's _djvu.txt), byte for byte; where a quoted sentence wraps in the scan, the two OCR lines are joined with one space. The archive.org scan of the maker's document counts as primary. Manual: 'The Fairchild Video Entertainment System' owner's booklet (archive.org item Fairchild-Channel-F-Manual). The manual also says: 'Do not pick up the Game Console by any of the wires that are permanently attached to it.'
controller_bays = 1: the manual describes ONE storage well under the dust cover in which both Hand-Controllers nest ('nest' the Hand-Controllers in their compartment).

Partial facts not filed as lists: the console has an 'On/Off' switch on the back, a 'Reset' button and the TIME / MODE / HOLD / START selector buttons, plus a 'Press To Eject' bar for the Videocart; the manual gives no complete console control list. Videocarts are inserted 'in much the same way as an 8-track audio cartridge' with 'the edge label facing towards you'; the face the slot is on is not stated, so media is not filed.
released: CHM gives '1976 (Made)', a manufacture date, not a launch date; null.
